headline: Relore combines repository decision history with current-code search; reported retrieval gains remain narrow
summary: A September 21, 2026 Hugging Face community article and the public relore repository describe a tool that indexes issue and pull-request history with author and trust metadata, then joins that history to current-code search in a maintained clone. Its project-authored, model-judged retrieval evaluation reports Recall@10 rising from 0.938 to 1.000 for 48 Transformers failure queries after query expansion, and from 0.375 to 0.475 for 40 precedent queries. The larger pooled rationale result is contaminated by same-thread answer leakage; the leak-free rationale slices are only 7 and 9 examples. In one author-reported Transformers case, relore found two existing fix threads and the agent avoided writing another patch; a code-browsing overview reportedly used about 5% of the tokens needed to read a whole file. These results support bounded accounts of retrieval and one field case, not a general reduction in duplicate work, better patches or higher coding-agent productivity.
